newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU parliament heads towards BSE censure vote.
newsitem.headline: EU parliament heads towards BSE censure vote.

text.p: The European Parliament is moving towards a censure motion accusing the European Commission of mishandling the mad cow crisis, parliamentary sources said on Friday.

German Christian Democrat Reimer Boege, who chaired the parliament's inquiry into the handling of the crisis, now backs a censure vote unless the Commission improves its veterinary services and controls.
"The committee is toughening its stance," said one parliamentary source, referring to the special committee of inquiry into bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), known as mad cow disease.

Belgian Socialist Jose Happart, the most radical member of the 19-member cross-party committee, is pressing for an immediate vote on a censure motion which would need the backing of two-thirds of the parliament's 626 members to pass.
But Boege told Reuters by telephone he was pressing for a commitment to censure the Commission only if it did not meet the Committee's concerns within six months.
The committee is due to vote on February 5-6 on 254 amendments to a draft report presented this month by Spanish Socialist Manuel Medina Ortega.

The report accused Britain as well as the Commission of failings in fighting the fatal brain-wasting disease after London said in March 1996 there was a possibility that BSE could be transmitted to people who ate infected beef.
The parliament, flexing its new investigative powers under the Maastricht Treaty, opened the BSE inquiry in September.

European Commission President Jacques Santer said this week that the Commission will shortly make changes to meet criticism from the parliament, the European Union's only democratically elected institution.

Commission officials said the changes, including the creation of an independent food safety agency to be chaired by EU Consumer Affairs commissioner Emma Bonino, might be made before the committee voted.
The agency would bring responsibility for food safety under one roof rather than several at present. But it would separate responsibility for drafting farm legislation from ensuring food safety.
The European Parliament is due to vote on February 19 in full session in Strasbourg on the BSE inquiry report.
